subject: High-touch availability approval matrix for Echelon Health
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: High-touch availability approval matrix for Echelon Health

Team —

Echelon Health (strategic pilot deal) has come back with a request for a custom availability package: they want a written uptime commitment of 99.99% with a p95 generation latency target of <=200ms for their API traffic (US region) and an operational penalty/credit if we miss. They're also asking for dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) and an SLA-secured maintenance blackout window.

Summary of what they asked (from the attached spreadsheet):
- 99.99% uptime (monthly)
- p95 <= 200ms for text generation across average sequence lengths (payloads: 512 tokens typical)
- Dedicated pool in us-west-2 with failover to us-east-1
- 4 hr incident response, 1 hr urgent paging for sev1
- Credit formula with monthly cap (they suggested 10% monthly credits)

As this is flagged as a strategic account (pipeline: EH-2026-47), I need product + infra + finance to propose an "approval matrix" we can present: what we can commit to today, what requires product changes or ops runbook updates, and a recommended commercial uplift.

Please review the attached `echelon_slo_proposal.xlsx` and reply with:
1) Feasibility notes (can we hit p95 200ms on current runtime?)
2) Lead time and operational runbook changes for dedicated pools
3) Suggested financial uplift (monthly) and max credit exposure we can accept

I'd like to consolidate internal recommendations by EOD so we can share a concrete option set with Alex Turner.

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: echelon_slo_proposal.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-06-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High-touch availability approval matrix for Echelon Health

Thanks Grace — quick product-level thoughts:

- p95 200ms is aggressive at production scale for general-purpose workloads; achievable on dedicated pools for narrow models and careful request shaping, but depends heavily on concurrency profile and sequence length distribution.
- Need concrete expected QPS and peak concurrency from Echelon so we can model KV cache hit rates and batching behavior.
- We should offer a staged SLO: phase 1 (canary) target p95 <= 300ms, phase 2 (post-optimization) p95 <= 220ms, and a long-term commitment to explore 200ms with kernel/compilation tuning.
- The penalty formula they proposed (10% credits) seems high; we should cap cumulative credits per quarter and include a clear exclusion list (maintenance windows, customer-induced load spikes).

Please provide the traffic profile (typical qps, peak qps, average tokens per request, percent chat vs. single-turn generation). I'll draft a technical caveats doc (`slo_risks.md`) with options.

- Aditya
VP Product, Redwood Inference

Attachment: slo_risks.md (notes)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High-touch availability approval matrix for Echelon Health

Operational notes from infra/ops:

- Dedicated pool: we can provision a dedicated GPU pool in us-west-2. Typical lead time is ~10 business days for reserved capacity plus testing.
- Cost: preliminary estimate for the committed pool (sized for steady-state 150 qps / 1k concurrent token generation) is ~ $72k/month (infrastructure + ops overhead). That's before applied engineering/optimization work.
- Latency: with pre-warmed KV caches and steady-state batching tuned, p95 of ~250-300ms is realistic for medium models (7B). 200ms will likely require a combination of lighter model selection (4-6B), aggressive quantization, and bespoke kernel/compilation tuning.
- Reliability: we can support 99.99% availability across the dedicated pool if we commit to cross-region failover and a standby capacity reserve (15%). That increases cost.

Constraints / items needing clarity:
1) Exact traffic profile (qps and token distribution)
2) Which models they expect to use (catalog/model size)
3) Acceptance of staged rollout (canary -> regional rollout -> global)

Recommend: provide 2 commercial options (Gold: 99.99% + p95 <= 250ms with dedicated pool + 30% uplift; Silver: 99.95% + p95 <= 350ms with lower uplift). I'll attach the runbook excerpt for dedicated pools.

Monica Patel
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: dedicated_pool_runbook.pdf (runbook excerpt)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@echelonhealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High-touch availability approval matrix for Echelon Health

Alex — thanks for the initial ask. Quick alignment note from Redwood:

We can outline two concrete paths that balance latency, availability, and commercial terms:

Option A (Gold) — recommended
- Availability: 99.99% monthly uptime
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms (initial); targeted engineering work to approach <=220ms within 90 days
- Dedicated pool (us-west-2) + cross-region failover
- Commercial uplift: ~30% over standard committed pricing; capped monthly credit exposure to 5% of monthly invoice
- Lead time: ~2 weeks to provision and test

Option B (Silver) — lower risk
- Availability: 99.95%
- Latency: p95 <= 350ms
- Lower dedicated pool footprint, lower uplift (15%)
- Faster lead time

Could you share the traffic profile (avg qps, peak qps, typical tokens per request) so we can size pools precisely and provide a final number? Grace will share an approval matrix from internal stakeholders by EOD.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T16:25:00-07:00
Subject: Approval matrix and decision (internal) — Echelon Health

Team — consolidating the inputs and authorizing an internal recommendation. See attached `approval_matrix_v1.csv` (summary) and `billing_surcharge_calc.pdf`.

Decision (internal recommendation to present to customer):
- Approve Option A (Gold) as the customer-facing offering with the following modifications:
  * Latency commitment: p95 <= 250ms initial, with a defined 90-day optimization window to target <=220ms. We will not commit to 200ms in the contract at signing.
  * Uptime: 99.99% with a quarterly credit cap of 5% monthly invoice for any validated downtime outside agreed maintenance windows.
  * Dedicated pool: provisioned in us-west-2 with cross-region failover; 15% standby reserve required.
  * Commercial uplift: 30% on committed capacity, and a 2x surcharge on emergency incident on-call outside of standard maintenance windows.

Operational preconditions (must be included in SOW):
- Customer to provide full traffic profile and chosen models 5 business days prior to provisioning.
- Two-week canary with SLIs instrumented and runbook approved by infra.
- Legal to sign off on credit cap language and exclusions.

Next steps: Rishi to send the customer-facing option set today. Legal/Finance to draft the commercial addendum (I'll loop in legal). Monica to add runbook steps to the dedicated pool playbook.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Infrastructure Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: approval_matrix_v1.csv, billing_surcharge_calc.pdf
